name: MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.CAR.existsNaimarkCounterexampleOfDensity_continuum
title: A Naimark counterexample of continuum norm density

content.display_title: A Naimark counterexample of continuum norm density
content.one_sentence_role: Gives a C*-algebra of norm density $\mathfrak c$ whose nonzero irreducible representations form one unitary-equivalence class, without an identification with the compact operators.
content.natural_language_statement: There exist a nonzero complex C*-algebra $B$, not required to be unital, a complex Hilbert space $K$, and a nonzero irreducible $*$-representation $\sigma:B\to B(K)$ with the following properties. Every nonzero irreducible $*$-representation of $B$ is unitarily equivalent to $\sigma$. The representation $\sigma$ is not both injective and surjective onto $\mathcal K(K)$, the full algebra of compact operators on $K$. Finally, $$\operatorname{dens}_{\|\cdot\|}(B)=\mathfrak c,\qquad\mathfrak c=2^{\aleph_0}.$$ Here density refers to the norm topology. None of the representations is required in advance to preserve an identity.
content.assumptions: This is an existence theorem with no CH hypothesis. Its statement allows nonunital C*-algebras and places no requirement on the existence of a faithful representation on a separable Hilbert space.
content.conclusion: One may take $B=T=C^*(\pi(A)\cup\{L_i:i\in I\})$, where $A$ is CAR, $\pi$ is the selected GNS direct sum, and $L_i$ are the unitaries from the fixed homogeneity and shell construction. Take $K=\mathcal H$ and $\sigma=\rho_0$, the inclusion of this concrete algebra in $B(\mathcal H)$. Thus the constructed example is unital, even though unitality is not required by the existence statement.
content.proof_summary: Use the constructed algebra $T$ and its inclusion representation $\rho_0$. The classification theorem gives the single unitary-equivalence class, the compact-operator exclusion applies to $\rho_0$, and the density theorem gives the required value $\mathfrak c$.

proof_steps.text: Take the algebra $T$, its selected GNS direct sum $\mathcal H$, and the inclusion $\rho_0$. The representation-classification theorem says that $\rho_0$ is nonzero irreducible and that, for any nonzero irreducible $*$-representation $\rho:T\to B(H)$, a unitary $U:\mathcal H\to H$ satisfies $U\rho_0(t)=\rho(t)U$. This statement does not require $\rho(1)=I_H$ as an initial assumption.

The compact-operator exclusion rules out every injective representation of $T$ onto the full algebra of compact operators, in particular the specified inclusion $\rho_0$. The density theorem gives $\operatorname{dens}_{\|\cdot\|}(T)=\mathfrak c$. These are precisely the other conditions of the existential predicate in the Lean statement.

content.lean_realization_notes: The fixed example also admits a faithful representation on a separable Hilbert space, but that is not a condition in this existence statement and is not asserted for every C*-algebra satisfying it.
